title: Failure concordance layer and telemetry bridge for inference errors
creator: Ava K. Martinez
description: Create a canonical failure concordance layer that maps raw inference signals (HTTP/gRPC status codes, client and server timeouts, overload/backpressure indicators, OOMs, model runtime errors, token-generation rejects, and model quality regressions) into a compact, queryable taxonomy. Implement a telemetry bridge that enriches traces, metrics, and logs with the concordance classification so dashboards, alerts, and downstream analytics can operate on a unified error vocabulary. Deliverables: (1) spec for classification labels and span/log attributes, (2) enforcement points (ingest enrichment, tracing hooks, sidecar enrichers), (3) metric/label design for low-cardinality SLIs and high-cardinality trace payloads, and (4) a set of Grafana dashboards and LogQL queries for SLOs, incident triage, and per-model failure slices.
acceptance_criteria: Specification doc published in Confluence with mapping table for raw signals -> canonical classes
Tracing hooks instrumented in runtime and SDKs to emit rw.failure.class and rw.failure.reason attributes
Ingress pipeline enrichment (log processor) tags traces/logs within 200ms and persists raw failure payload to raw logs store
Low-cardinality Prometheus metrics exported for SLI aggregation (failure_class_total with labels {class, route, model_family})
Dashboards with drilldown links from failure-class tiles to trace viewer, raw logs, and affected model/version lists
Canary rollout on 10% of Prod traffic with regression checks and rollback playbook
tasks: Draft classification schema and vocabulary (timeout, overload, model-exec, model-reject, decode-error, client-abort, transport-4xx/5xx)
Prototype span attribute rw.failure.* in serving runtime and python/js SDKs
Add enrichment stage to log pipeline (Loki) and ensure trace ID propagation to raw logs
Create Prometheus exporter changes and low-cardinality metric names
Design Grafana dashboards and LogQL queries for exploratory triage
Write rollout plan with canary thresholds and SLO/alert definitions
Run internal eval using synthetic traces and real traffic replay to validate classification precision
notes: 2025-02-19 - Kickoff: aligned on single canonical label set; avoid >20 classes to keep metrics usable
2025-02-22 - Decision: use two-tier approach — low-cardinality metric labels for SLOs + free-text failure_reason in logs for triage
2025-02-27 - Security review considered: no PII expected in failure_reason but logs pipeline must mask request payloads; deferred required controls to telemetry infra team
2025-03-01 - Infra feedback: high-cardinality labels on Prometheus will increase TSDB costs. Agreed to emit cardinality-limited labels and push full vectors to raw logs/trace event store
2025-03-03 - Design review with PM/DS: add model_family and route as optional top-level labels; model_version only available in trace payloads to avoid churn in metrics
2025-03-05 - Implementation: runtime PR merged for span attribute; SDK patches in review; log enrich pipeline staged to staging cluster
comments: 2025-02-20 - Ravi S. Patel: Draft spec looks good. Need to ensure SDKs have backward-compatible attribute names.
2025-02-24 - Lina Zhao (SRE): Suggest adding a sampling rule to always sample traces where failure_class != null to aid post-mortem.
2025-03-02 - Priya Menon (PM): Highlight that we must expose per-customer failure rates to support enterprise SLAs; add as follow-up if privacy controls approved.
2025-03-04 - Engineering review: Prototype shows 0.6% p95 latency increase when doing inline enrichment; moving enrichment to async pipeline stage reduces overhead to <0.1%
2025-03-05 - QA: Staging test passed for classification accuracy on synthetic corpus (precision 0.93, recall 0.89)
risks: Increased cardinality in Prometheus leading to higher storage/ingest costs
Misclassification of model errors (false positives) leading to noisy alerts
Trace propagation gaps from third-party client SDKs causing blind spots
Compliance: raw failure_payload may include sensitive prompt text — requires masking in logs
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Staging: instrument runtime and pipeline against staging traffic; validate precision/recall
Phase 1 - Canary (10%): enable low-cardinality metrics and trace-level enrichment for single region; monitor latency and SLI impact
Phase 2 - Gradual (50%): expand to multi-region routes with increased sampling for failures
Phase 3 - Full: enable for all customers with tenant opt-in for raw failure payload retention
follow_up: ENG-30567: link to operational failure lens (post-rollout) for automated runbooks
PM-412: product request for per-customer SLA dashboards (requires privacy gating)
DES-214: UX for failure-class drilldown in Console route view
